_comment: Single source of truth for the Open Play Brick rev B wiring. The emulator draws its diagram from this file, tools/gen_pins.mjs generates firmware/core/pins.h from it, and tools/gen_build_doc.mjs generates the parts list and wiring table in docs/BUILD.md from it, so the picture, the simulation, the firmware and the instructions cannot drift apart.

board.name: Open Play Brick
board.note: Rev B is the module build: off-the-shelf breakout boards around an Adafruit ESP32-C6 Feather. A brick-sized board would use the same chips and the same GPIO numbers.

NFC_BUSY.desc: PN5180 BUSY handshake, high while the reader works

NFC_RST.desc: PN5180 reset. Held low it puts the reader in hard power-down, which is how it is switched off for sleep

I2C_SDA.desc: I2C data, 400 kHz. On the Feather this is the STEMMA QT connector

IMU_INT1.desc: Motion interrupt. Wakes the MCU from deep sleep (GPIO0 to 7 can do that on the ESP32-C6)

PERIPH_EN.desc: High = pixels powered and amplifier enabled. Low in sleep

LAMP_EN.desc: High = the white LED beside the colour sensor is lit

QT_PWR.desc: Feather only: powers the STEMMA QT connector. Held high, including in sleep, so the accelerometer can wake the brick

I2S_BCLK.desc: I2S bit clock, 16 kHz x 64. Shared by the amplifier and the microphone, and runs whenever the brick is awake

I2S_DOUT.desc: I2S data to the amplifier, left slot

I2S_DIN.desc: I2S data from the microphone, left slot

USB_DP.desc: USB D+ (built-in USB Serial/JTAG: flashing and console)

PIX_GND.desc: Ground return of the pixels, through the load switch. Open in sleep

parts.name: ESP32-C6
parts.package: on the Feather; QFN-32, 5 x 5 mm as a bare chip
parts.why: RISC-V MCU with Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5 and 802.15.4 radios and built-in USB. It has seven more GPIOs than the ESP32-C3, which is what makes room for the microphone and a proper reset line for the reader.

buy.note: Also contains the fuel gauge (U5), regulator (U7), charger (U8) and USB-C socket (J1).

parts.name: PN5180
parts.package: module with antenna; HVQFN-40, 6 x 6 mm as a bare chip
parts.why: Full-power NFC frontend with ISO 15693 support. Already shown to read these tags in the Ellerbach project.

buy.sku: Elechouse PN5180, or a generic PN5180 board
buy.note: The one part Adafruit does not sell. Pad names differ between makers: see step 6.

parts.name: Loop antenna
parts.why: Tags are read on the face of this coil. One coil cannot tell where on the brick a tag sits.

parts.name: LIS3DH
parts.package: STEMMA QT breakout; LGA, 3 x 3 mm as a bare chip
parts.why: 3-axis, a few microamps in wake-on-motion mode, with an interrupt output that wakes the MCU. The smaller LIS2DH12 has the same registers.

parts.name: TCS34725
parts.package: breakout with a white LED; FN-6, 2 x 2.4 mm as a bare chip
parts.why: RGB + clear light-to-digital converter with an IR filter. The breakout carries the white LED that lights whatever is in front of it.

buy.item: TCS34725 colour sensor breakout with on-board white LED and LED pin
buy.note: Adafruit's own board (1334) is retired, but copies of it are sold widely. Check that yours has a pad marked LED.

parts.name: MAX17048
parts.why: Reports cell voltage, state of charge and charge rate over I2C, so the firmware knows the battery level and whether it is charging.

parts.name: MAX98357A
parts.package: breakout; TQFN-16, 3 x 3 mm as a bare chip
parts.why: Digital audio in, speaker out, no DAC needed.

parts.name: Speaker
parts.why: Small enough to tuck in, large enough to be heard.

buy.item: Small speaker, 4 to 8 ohm, 1 to 3 W
buy.note: Cut off any plug and put the bare wires in the amplifier's screw terminal.

to.+/-: amplifier screw terminal, either way round

parts.name: ICS-43434
parts.package: breakout; 3.5 x 2.65 mm as a bare chip
parts.why: Digital MEMS microphone that shares the amplifier's clocks, so it costs one GPIO. The firmware only measures loudness to hear a clap. It does not record, store or send audio.

buy.note: An INMP441 board wires the same way.

parts.name: RGB pixels x 8
parts.package: NeoPixel stick, 51 x 10 mm; SK6805-EC15, 1.5 mm each as bare parts
parts.why: Addressable RGB LEDs on one data wire.

parts.name: Load switch
parts.package: MOSFET driver board; a load-switch IC on a brick-sized board
parts.why: Cuts power to the pixels in sleep. Eight idle pixels draw about 8 mA, which would flatten the battery in two or three days. Optional: without it the pixels wire straight to BAT and GND.

buy.item: Adafruit MOSFET driver, STEMMA JST PH
buy.note: Recommended. It switches the ground side of the pixel stick. Add its 3-pin JST PH cable when you order.

parts.name: 3.3 V regulator
parts.why: 500 mA peak, enough for the reader's transmit bursts.

parts.name: Li-Po charger
parts.why: Charges the cell whenever USB is plugged in.

parts.name: Li-Po cell
parts.package: 500 mAh pouch with JST-PH plug, 29 x 36 x 4.75 mm
parts.why: Plugs straight into the Feather. Has its own protection circuit.

buy.note: If you use another brand, check the plug polarity against the + mark on the Feather before connecting.

parts.name: USB-C
parts.why: Charging, flashing and serial console over one port.

extras.item: STEMMA QT cable, 50 or 100 mm (Feather to accelerometer)
STEMMA QT to male pins cable (accelerometer to colour sensor)
